title: No one may rightly claim justification without heartfelt renunciation of worldly vices
source_text: III. Primum ergo apud nos certum atque constitutum est neminem legitime & vere statuere posse, se a peccatis suis coram Deo justificatum, seque Deo gratum esse & acceptum ad vitam aeternam, nisi qui ex corde vitiis & cupiditatibus mundanis renuntiaverit, ut juxta quam nos docet gratia Evangelica, sobrie, pie & juste in praesenti saeculo vivat. Ac proinde quicunque in peccatis suis haerent, & indulgent carnis affectibus, quantumlibet fidem Christi profitentur, & assensum aliquem Evangelicae Veritati praebeant, si quacunque ratione in animum suum inducant se apud Deum esse misericordiam consecutos, Deumque sibi in Christo placatum & propitium esse, proculdubio mera est haec fallacia Satanae, & securitas carnalis atque perniciosissima: Nec enim remissio peccatorum promittitur, ac misericordia & gratia divina offertur, nisi illis qui serio resipiscunt, & peccata sua non modo confitentur, sed etiam deserunt. Juxta illud Salomonis, Qui abscondit scelera sua non prosperabitur; qui autem confessus fuerit, & reliquerit ea, misericordiam consequetur.
pass_a_gloss: First, then, it is certain and settled among us that no one can lawfully and truly establish that he has been justified from his sins before God, and that he is pleasing to God and accepted to eternal life, except one who has from the heart renounced vices and worldly desires, so that he may live soberly, piously, and justly in the present age according to what evangelical grace teaches us. And therefore whoever remain in their sins and indulge fleshly affections, however much they profess the faith of Christ and give some assent to evangelical truth, if by any reason they bring their mind to think they have obtained mercy with God and that God is appeased and propitious to them in Christ, this is beyond doubt a mere deceit of Satan and a carnal and most pernicious security: for remission of sins is not promised, nor is divine mercy and grace offered, except to those who seriously repent and not only confess but also desert their sins. According to that of Solomon: He who hides his crimes will not prosper; but he who has confessed and forsaken them will obtain mercy.
pass_b_english: Reformed doctrine first denies lawful assurance to anyone still clinging to unrepented vice.
Claims of pardon without serious repentance are Satanic security, not gospel mercy.
